doc.raw:
Package domain holds the shared vocabulary of the lending library: books,
members, loans, and the errors that every layer returns.

Domain types hold data and small pure rules. They import nothing else in
the module, so every other package can use them.
doc.summary: Package domain holds the shared vocabulary of the lending library: books, members, loans, and the errors that every layer returns.

doc.raw:
Package service holds the lending rules. It checks each request and calls
storage in the right order.
doc.summary: Package service holds the lending rules.

description.text: Package service holds the lending rules. It checks each request and calls storage in the right order.

doc.raw:
Package store defines the storage contracts that the services use. Two
stores implement them: [memory.Store] and [filestore.Store].

Every store follows these rules:

 1. ctx comes first.
 2. Values go in and out, never shared pointers.
 3. Errors wrap the sentinels in package domain, such as [domain.ErrNotFound].

A typical read:

	b, err := s.Book(ctx, id)
	if errors.Is(err, domain.ErrNotFound) { … }
